info.desc: Isn't Anything is the debut full-length studio album by My Bloody Valentine, released in November 1988 on Creation Records. After the band's original vocalist Dave Conway left in 1987, to be replaced by Bilinda Butcher, the band continued for a while in their previous noisy indie-pop style before Kevin Shields returned to their avant-garde roots, and began to explore the possibilities offered by the studio facilities available after signing to Creation Records in 1988. The first fruits of this experimentation was the single/EP "You Made Me Realise", released in July 1988, with Isn't Anything following later that year. Most of .

podcast.body: Released in 1988, this album, along with the "You Made Me Realise" EP, marked a significant period for the band. Released only four months apart, these two works showcased My Bloody Valentine beginning to find their distinctive sound, characterized by extreme experimentation with guitars, extensive use of effects pedals, and the integration of noise as a natural component of their music. These works were very well received within the community and were considered the almost official starting point for the emerging sound of Shoegaze. "Estos trabajos fueron muy bien acogidos dentro de la comunidad y serían considerados como el punto de partida casi oficial de este sonido que estaba emergiendo. El Show Guys."

podcast.body: Released in 1988, this record is considered to have arrived "at the very beginning of the whole shoegaze thing." It was characterized by "guitar drones and layers and layers of feedback" that generated a "near-trance-like soundscape," an "impenetrable atmosphere of sound," and made extensive use of effects pedals. "In 1988, they released a record called, Isn't Anything, which was filled with guitar drones and layers and layers of feedback that created near-translikes soundscape."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
